links: Dense 1.6 bar air slows molecular diffusion
Scent trails persist 1.6× longer in still night air

skill.effect: Tracks scent trails for 15s, reveals hidden eggs and carrion markers.

chains.weakness: Loud noises disrupt tracking; sensitive to strong chemical sprays.

journal.en: They don't hunt by sight. The thick air carries the salt and decay where the eyes fail.

plausibility.summary: Nocturnal shore foraging on carrion and eggs fits F16/D18: still night air and fog-prone dawns extend scent usability when F20 turbidity and moonless nights (F6) weaken vision. A tactile, mobile rhinarium is a standard tetrapod solution for close-range chemotaxis without large eyes. At 15 cm, diffusion-limited scent patches in wrack lines are a real search problem worth specialized rostral tissue.

chains.trait: Hinged jaw with calcite-softening salivary glands
links: Mechanical cracking is energetically costly in 1.05 g gravity
Evolved acidic saliva to dissolve calcium carbonate shells

skill.effect: Sprays acidic saliva on target, breaks defense in 8s, leaves sour taste.

chains.weakness: Saliva depletes quickly; using it on bone yields no extra nutrients.

journal.en: They melt stone to reach the white inside. A clever trick, until the acid burns their own tongue.

plausibility.summary: Target thin intertidal egg chorions or low-calcite spawn collars (not thick avian eggs). Chain root: jaw force vs shell thickness + D25 energy cost, not F2 alone. Saliva = mild acid (pH ~4–5) plus proteases; paired weakness: keratinized tongue/gum linings or brief bursts only (already in lore).

chains.trait: Splayed forelimbs with keratinized gripping pads
links: Shore habitat features wet, slick basalt and tidal scour
High wind force per m/s pushes light bodies
Low center of gravity and strong grip essential

skill.effect: Climbs vertical wet surfaces in 4s, escapes grapples and falls safely.

chains.weakness: Pads lose adhesion in dry, dusty highlands; vulnerable to heatstroke inland.

journal.en: Wet stone would fling them off, but their feet stick like damp paper. A shore-born grip.

plausibility.summary: Low-profile shore tetrapod on slick basalt during F13 tidal scour and F19/D17 gale fits selection for wide stance, low centre of mass, and wet-surface adhesion. Dense air (F4) makes aerial escape costly for a 0.7 kg body, so clinging and crevice refuge are honest. Inland dry heat failure is the expected specialist trade-off.

chains.trait: Ampullae-like electroreceptors in snout and forelimbs
links: Nocturnal tide pools have low visibility and turbid water
Mechanical vibration and bioelectric fields reveal trapped prey
Evolved electroreceptive pits to detect heartbeats and struggling larvae

skill.effect: Pulses ground/water, reveals hidden targets in 6s radius, stuns if too close.

chains.weakness: Useless on dry land; electrical storms cause temporary confusion.

journal.en: They listen to the water's pulse. In the dark, every heartbeat is a drum.

plausibility.summary: Keep passive pits for tide-pool and damp wrack only; skill = short-range reveal of hidden eggs/invertebrates, no discharge. Drop stun or gate it as ‘highly speculative’ optional deep-secret. Observe behaviour: snout pressed to water, freeze on wave noise (vibration masking), not rhythmic paw ‘pulses’.

relations.note: Ambushes near wrack lines where rastrons crack eggs.
Snatches stray juveniles during spring tide openings.

secrets: Find a tide pool with a cluster of pale eggs to unlock the 'Shell Soften' move early.
Spot one standing perfectly still on a vertical spray-slick cliff to reveal 'Grip Climb'.
moments: On a moonless night, a cluster of them presses against a wet basalt wall, snouts trembling in unison, reading the silent language of decay and salt.

journal.en: The tide recedes, leaving treasures in the dark.
They steal the future, one softened shell at a time.
